[LLM] AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) Hit from Developer / Non-EC2 Endpoint (Nx Console Credential Theft) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects outbound connections to the AWS Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) from endpoints that are not EC2 instances. The Nx Console v18.95.0 payload probes IMDS to steal IAM role credentials — a developer laptop or non-AWS workstation contacting IMDS is a strong credential-access signal. Rationale: The article and external corroboration (The Hacker News, CyberSecurityNews, GBHackers) call out `Connections to AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) from non-AWS environments` as a documented IOC of the Nx Console payload's credential-stealing stage. The 169.254.169.254 link-local address has only one legitimate use (EC2/IMDS); any hit from a Mac/Linux laptop or developer workstation is anomalous. Sigma is omitted because the detection requires asset-class context (non-EC2) that single-event Sigma cannot express cleanly. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/ • https://gbhackers.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension/
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1078.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let DevEndpoints = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, DeviceCategory, OSPlatform, DeviceType, IsInternetFacing) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | where DeviceCategory != "Server" or isempty(DeviceCategory);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
| where RemotePort in (80,443,8080)
| join kind=inner DevEndpoints on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, DeviceCategory, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
| where DstPortNumber in (80,443,8080)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkBytes, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog OR source:osquery) (@DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @network.destination.ip:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationHostname:*169.254.169.254*) -@host.tags:cloud_provider\:aws
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.169.254" RemotePort=/^(80|443|8080)$/ | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.src_ip) as src_ip values(All_Traffic.app) as app values(All_Traffic.process_name) as process_name values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip="169.254.169.254" AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080) NOT (All_Traffic.src_category IN ("aws-ec2","aws_instance","ec2")) by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where count > 0 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.src_ip) as src_ip values(All_Traffic.app) as app values(All_Traffic.process_name) as process_name values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip="169.254.169.254" AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (80,443,8080) NOT (All_Traffic.src_category IN ("aws-ec2","aws_instance","ec2")) by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where count > 0 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or SHA1 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1") or MD5 in~ ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__HASH_LIST__` placeholder with article-specific SHA256
    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive hash match
level: critical
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("1a4afce34918bdc74ae3f31edaffffaa0ee074d83618f53edfd88137927340b8", "b0cefb66b953e5184b6adb3035e9e267335ac5eabfe1848e07834777b9397b74", "e7347d90653efc565f03733a95e9209d78f9cfa81e31ff2b2dd9d48d75a4b8b1")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]

[LLM] OCI image extraction creates symlink with absolute path target (CWE-61 primitive) Exploitation High
Detects the Boxlite OCI layer extractor creating symlinks during tar processing where the link target points outside the staging directory (absolute path under /etc, /root, /home, /var/spool/cron, etc.). This is the core CVE-2026-46703 primitive — the unvalidated symlink target in apply_oci_layer() that turns a subsequent regular-file tar entry into an arbitrary host file write. Rationale: Article names the vulnerable binary explicitly (boxlite) and the exploit primitive's effect (writes outside dest staging dir into host paths like /etc/passwd, /root/.ssh/authorized_keys). The detection pivots on these two facts together — a high-fidelity pair because legitimate Boxlite extraction only writes inside its staging directory (typically /tmp/<sandbox-id>/ or /var/lib/boxlite/), never into /etc or /root. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f396-4rp4-7v2j
ATT&CKT1611 T1574 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "boxlite"
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated", "SymbolicLinkCreated")
| where FolderPath startswith "/etc/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/root/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/home/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/var/spool/cron/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/etc/cron.d/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
   or FolderPath startswith "/etc/systemd/system/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "boxlite"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("symlink", "symlinkat", "linkat")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/etc/", "/root/", "/home/", "/var/spool/cron", "/etc/cron.d", "/etc/sudoers.d", "/etc/systemd/system")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, ProcessID, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Boxlite sandbox writes to SSH authorized_keys (post-exploit RCE pivot) Installation High
Detects the Boxlite service writing to any authorized_keys file on the host — the article explicitly calls out this technique as the RCE pivot ('writing the attacker's public key into the host's authorized_keys'). Since Boxlite has no legitimate reason to touch user SSH key files outside its sandboxed Box filesystems, any such write is high-confidence post-exploitation of CVE-2026-46703. Rationale: Article body explicitly cites this technique: 'The attacker can further leverage this capability to achieve remote code execution, such as writing the attacker's public key into the host's authorized_keys.' Boxlite is a container sandbox — it has zero legitimate workflow that involves writing to /root/.ssh/ or /home/*/.ssh/ on the host, making this a clean alerting signal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f396-4rp4-7v2j

[LLM] Vulnerable Twig package (CVE-2026-46633) installed (twig/twig < 3.26.0) Exploitation High
Surface assets where Microsoft Defender TVM reports the Twig PHP templating library at a version vulnerable to CVE-2026-46633. Exploitation gives RCE via single-quote injection in a `{% use %}` template name; SecurityPolicy allows `{% use %}` even under sandbox, so any application that accepts attacker-influenced template names against twig/twig < 3.26.0 is reachable. Prioritise patching to 3.26.0 or later. Rationale: Article is a vendor advisory: identifies the exact package (composer:twig/twig), fixed version (3.26.0), and CVE (CVE-2026-46633). The only high-fidelity, non-generic detection from this content is asset coverage — every other behaviour-based UC (PHP web server spawning shells, web-shell cache file writes) collapses into generic web-shell rules already shipped, which the prompt explicitly excludes. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7p85-w9px-jpjp

[LLM] AWS IAM role trust policy created with set-qualified operator on GitHub OIDC sub claim Installation High
Hunts the exact misconfiguration class that @hulumi/policies <1.3.2 failed to flag: CreateRole/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy CloudTrail events whose trust policy uses ForAnyValue:StringLike / ForAllValues:StringLike / ForAllValues:StringEquals against token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub. Any role created with this shape — particularly with wildcards in the sub value — is assumable by GitHub Actions workflows the role owner never intended to authorize. Rationale: Article specifies the exact unsafe pattern: set-qualified operators (ForAnyValue:StringLike etc.) applied to token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub bypass the inspector. CloudTrail's CreateRole/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy carries the full policyDocument as JSON — substring matching for both the operator family AND the OIDC sub claim string is high-fidelity because the combination is essentially never seen in correctly-authored trust policies (canonical pattern is the bare StringLike or StringEquals). Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/avoiding-mistakes-with-aws-oidc-integration-conditions • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_condition_operators.html • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/deployment/security-hardening-your-deployments/configuring-openid-connect-in-amazon-web-services
ATT&CKT1098.003 T1199 T1078.004

[LLM] AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity from GitHub OIDC with unexpected repo/branch sub claim Exploitation Medium
Downstream hunt for actor abuse of a role whose unsafe trust policy slipped past @hulumi/policies <1.3.2. Pivots on sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events where the WebIdentity issuer is token.actions.githubusercontent.com and the asserted sub claim does not match the org's approved GitHub repo allowlist — flagging the first-time-seen repo+role pairs that an attacker exploiting a wildcard sub policy would generate. Rationale: The article's bypass directly enables GitHub Actions OIDC sub-claim impersonation against IAM roles. AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is the actor-observable consequence — the userIdentity.userName field on the CloudTrail event carries the asserted sub (e.g. repo:owner/repo:ref:refs/heads/main). Anti-joining against an approved-org/repo lookup is the cleanest baseline-deviation pivot for catching exploitation of an unsafe policy that the scanner missed. Cross-referenced with the AWS GitHub OIDC docs and the Wiz misconfiguration write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/avoiding-mistakes-with-aws-oidc-integration-conditions • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/deployment/security-hardening-your-deployments/configuring-openid-connect-in-amazon-web-services

[LLM] CVE-2026-46614: Unauthorized /fission-function/ invocation on Fission router public listener (port 8888) Exploitation High
Detects HTTP requests to the internal-style /fission-function/<ns>/<name> route on the Fission router's public listener (svc/router, port 8888). On versions <= 1.22.0 this route is mounted on the public listener and allows any caller reaching the router to invoke any Function object — bypassing HTTPTrigger host/path/method restrictions. Post-fix (v1.23.0+), this path should only exist on port 8889 (svc/router-internal, ClusterIP-only), so any hit on port 8888 is either an unpatched cluster being exploited or an enumeration probe. Rationale: The path string `/fission-function/` and port 8888 are both directly named in the GHSA advisory as the vulnerable surface (pkg/router/httpTriggers.go:280-284 and svc/router listener config). After v1.23.0 this path should only appear on port 8889 (svc/router-internal), so hits on 8888 are unambiguous - either an exploitation attempt or an unpatched cluster still serving the route. We exclude 404 because that's enumeration covered by the next UC; 200 means successful unauthorized invocation, 502 means the function exists and went cold (still a successful enumeration). Defender KQL is empty because Fission runs on Linux K8s nodes and the relevant telemetry is HTTP-layer (ingress/WAF), not endpoint EDR. Falcon LogScale is empty for the same reason - FDR doesn't ship ingress HTTP path data. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/fission/fission/releases/tag/v1.23.0 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g33-6vg6-27m8
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Fission runs on Kubernetes (Linux) - this detection lives in ingress/WAF logs forwarded to CommonSecurityLog or web-tier IIS logs in front of the router
union isfuzzy=true
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has "/fission-function/"
  | where DestinationPort == 8888 or isempty(tostring(DestinationPort))
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, EventOutcome, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, RequestClientApplication
  | extend Verdict = case(EventOutcome has "200", "Successful unauthorized invocation", EventOutcome has "502", "Cold-start - function exists", EventOutcome has "404", "Probe miss", "Other - verify")
),
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriStem has "/fission-function/"
  | where sPort == 8888
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=cIP, DestinationIP=Computer, DestinationPort=sPort, RequestMethod=csMethod, RequestURL=strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?",csUriQuery), "")), EventOutcome=tostring(scStatus), DeviceVendor="Microsoft", DeviceProduct="IIS", RequestClientApplication=csUserAgent
  | extend Verdict = case(EventOutcome == "200", "Successful unauthorized invocation", EventOutcome == "502", "Cold-start - function exists", EventOutcome == "404", "Probe miss", "Other - verify")
)
| where Verdict != "Probe miss"   // 200/502 = signal; 404 alone is enumeration noise covered by UC2
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Fission Function Name Enumeration via /fission-function/ Probing (CVE-2026-46614 recon) Reconnaissance Medium
Detects function-name discovery against the Fission router by counting distinct /fission-function/<ns>/<name> paths probed from the same source within a short window. Per the advisory, callers can enumerate which functions exist by differentiating response semantics (404 = no such function, 200 = invoked, 502 = function exists and went cold). A burst of 404s interleaved with 200/502s from one source is the canonical recon shape. Rationale: The advisory explicitly calls out enumeration as an impact: 'Enumerate function names by probing the response semantics (404 vs 200 vs 502 from cold start).' Counting distinct paths under /fission-function/ per source IP in a short window directly models that pattern; requiring at least 3 404s alongside the path-count threshold filters legitimate trigger callers (who hit known paths and don't miss). Sigma is empty because this is a count/threshold detection, not single-event-shape. Defender and Falcon are empty because the telemetry sits at the ingress/WAF layer, not on endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/fission/fission/releases/tag/v1.23.0 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g33-6vg6-27m8
ATT&CKT1595.003 T1083
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let MinUniquePaths = 5;
let MinProbeMisses = 3;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
  | where RequestURL has "/fission-function/"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Router=DestinationIP
),
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
  | where csUriStem has "/fission-function/"
  | where sPort == 8888
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=cIP, RequestURL=csUriStem, Status=tostring(scStatus), UserAgent=csUserAgent, Router=Computer
)
| summarize
    UniqueFunctionPaths = dcount(RequestURL),
    TotalRequests = count(),
    HitFunctions = dcountif(RequestURL, Status in ("200","502")),
    MissFunctions = dcountif(RequestURL, Status == "404"),
    SamplePaths = make_set(RequestURL, 20),
    UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 5),
    Routers = make_set(Router, 3)
    by bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMinutes), SourceIP
| where UniqueFunctionPaths >= MinUniquePaths and MissFunctions >= MinProbeMisses
| extend EnumerationConfidence = case(
    HitFunctions > 0 and MissFunctions >= 3, "High - mixed 200/502 hits with 404 misses (likely successful enumeration)",
    MissFunctions >= 10, "Medium - heavy 404 probing",
    "Low")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:nginx OR source:kubernetes) @http.url_details.path:*/fission-function/*

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| where UniqueFunctionPaths >= 5 AND MissFunctions >= 3
| eval EnumerationConfidence=case(HitFunctions>0 AND MissFunctions>=3,"High - mixed 200/502 hits with 404 misses",MissFunctions>=10,"Medium - heavy 404 probing",true(),"Low")
| table _time, src, UniqueFunctionPaths, TotalRequests, HitFunctions, MissFunctions, EnumerationConfidence, Routers, UserAgents
| tstats summariesonly=false dc(Web.url) as UniqueFunctionPaths, count as TotalRequests, dc(eval(if(Web.status=="200" OR Web.status=="502", Web.url, null()))) as HitFunctions, dc(eval(if(Web.status=="404", Web.url, null()))) as MissFunctions, values(Web.http_user_agent) as UserAgents, values(Web.dest) as Routers from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*/fission-function/*" by _time span=10m, Web.src

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

[LLM] BadIIS rogue native module drop in IIS folders (demo.pdb / Chinese path heuristic) Installation Medium
Hunts non-trusted writes of DLL/native modules into IIS-served directories (\inetsrv\, \inetpub\wwwroot\bin\), and image loads by w3wp.exe of modules outside the canonical IIS install paths or whose file path contains Han/CJK characters. Targets the Talos-described BadIIS commodity variant whose modules carry 'demo.pdb' strings and Chinese-language folder paths. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'demo.pdb' strings and Chinese-language folder paths inside IIS binaries as the Talos-recommended hunt hooks. Standard EDR can't search PDB strings inline, so we proxy with (a) writes of native modules into IIS paths by non-installer processes and (b) the CJK Unicode range (\u4e00-\u9fff) in module paths, which catches the Chinese-folder-path signal directly. Memory mem-1304 already corroborated BadIIS as commodity MaaS infrastructure.
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1036.005

description: Detects file writes of DLL or EXE payloads into IIS-served directories (\inetsrv\, \inetpub\wwwroot\bin\) by a process that is NOT msiexec / TrustedInstaller / appcmd / drvinst. Aligns with Cisco Talos BadIIS commodity variant (May 2026) whose modules drop into IIS module paths and carry 'demo.pdb' strings.

[LLM] Talos weekly prevalent-malware hash hit (Coinminer worm / TunMirror / SECOH-QAD / KMS-Loader) Installation High
Hash IOC sweep for the five Talos-published prevalent-malware SHA256s for the week ending May 21 2026: Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe), PUA.Win.Tool.Tunmirror (TunMirror.exe), Win.Tool.Procpatcher (SECOH-QAD.exe), and the KM-prefixed sample. Covers process execution, file writes, and DLL/EXE module loads to surface infection regardless of stage. Rationale: Direct hash IOCs published by Cisco Talos with detection name + sample filename per hash. These are the week's top prevalent samples — VID001.exe (Coinminer worm), TunMirror.exe (network tunneling PUA), SECOH-QAD.exe (KMS-emulation tooling), KM-prefix loader. Hash equality is the highest-fidelity detection shape possible. [LLM] BadIIS traffic-hijacking: IIS 503 surge + anomalous external redirect ratio per site/hour Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Talos-described BadIIS impact pattern: hijacked IIS servers throwing 503 spikes (proxy/upstream failure) while also emitting an unusually high ratio of 30x/redirect responses pointing visitors to attacker-controlled SEO-fraud destinations. Aggregates per site per hour and flags hours that materially deviate from the per-site baseline. Rationale: Article explicitly tells defenders to 'actively monitor IIS environments for unauthorized traffic redirection, unexpected reverse proxying, or sudden spikes in 503 Service Unavailable errors' — this query is a direct expression of that guidance, anchored on per-site/per-hour anomalies versus a 30-day baseline so it doesn't fire on legitimately redirect-heavy sites. Datadog and Falcon LogScale fields left empty because raw IIS W3C access logs are not part of the standard FDR feed and are not in the Datadog source list provided.
ATT&CKT1496 T1565.002 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let lookback = 7d;
let bucket = 1h;
let BadIISSignals = W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where csMethod in~ ("GET","HEAD","POST")
| summarize Total = count(),
           Status503 = countif(scStatus == 503),
           Status3xx = countif(scStatus between (300 .. 399)),
           DistinctClients = dcount(cIP),
           DistinctURIs = dcount(csUriStem),
           SampleUserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5),
           SampleReferers = make_set(csReferer, 5)
           by Computer, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, bucket)
| extend PctErr503 = round((Status503 * 100.0) / Total, 2),
         PctRedirect = round((Status3xx * 100.0) / Total, 2)
| where (Status503 >= 50 and PctErr503 >= 20) or (Status3xx >= 100 and PctRedirect >= 40);
let Baseline = W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(lookback))
| summarize BaselineTotal = count(),
           BaselineRedirect = countif(scStatus between (300 .. 399)),
           Baseline503 = countif(scStatus == 503)
           by Computer, sSiteName
| extend BaselinePctRedirect = round((BaselineRedirect * 100.0) / BaselineTotal, 2),
         BaselinePctErr503 = round((Baseline503 * 100.0) / BaselineTotal, 2);
BadIISSignals
| join kind=leftouter Baseline on Computer, sSiteName
| where PctRedirect >= (coalesce(BaselinePctRedirect, 0.0) * 3) or PctErr503 >= (coalesce(BaselinePctErr503, 0.0) * 3)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, Total, Status503, Status3xx, PctErr503, PctRedirect, BaselinePctRedirect, BaselinePctErr503, DistinctClients, DistinctURIs, SampleUserAgents, SampleReferers
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

5 Supply Chain Attacks in 48 Hours: Why Securing One Layer Is Not Enough

StepSecurity
2026-05-21 10 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A poisoned VS Code extension breached GitHub. A trojanized PyPI package hit Microsoft. Compromised GitHub Actions and a self-spreading npm worm targeted thousands more. In just 48 hours, attackers hit every layer of the software development pipeline. Traditional security tools did not stop any of it.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Compromised Nx Console VS Code extension (nrwl.angular-console v18.94.0/18.95.0/18.100.0) install on endpoint
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Known Shai-Hulud / Nx Console implant hash match (SHA256/SHA1) · [LLM] macOS LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist persistence pointing at Python interpreter · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match

Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Nx Console / Shai-Hulud C2 connection (t.m-kosche.com, check.git-service.com, filev2.getsession.org, api.masscan.cloud, 83.142.209.194) · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Developer credential store read by Python or Node spawned from VS Code (Nx Console stealer pattern) · [LLM] GitHub audit log bulk private-repo clone burst (post Nx Console compromise pattern)
[LLM] Compromised Nx Console VS Code extension (nrwl.angular-console v18.94.0/18.95.0/18.100.0) install on endpoint Delivery High
Detects writes/installations of the malicious Nx Console extension versions published to the VS Code Marketplace on May 18, 2026. Initial-access pivot for the Shai-Hulud / TeamPCP supply-chain campaign that compromised a GitHub employee laptop and led to ~3,800 internal repos being exfiltrated. Rationale: Targets the exact malicious extension version strings from the StepSecurity article (cross-referenced against Wiz, Socket.dev, and JFrog vendor write-ups in session memory observations 1281, 1284, 1287); developer endpoints almost never receive a freshly published Nx Console version within hours of release so the temporal-uniqueness of these specific versions makes this very low FP. We also covered the two neighbour versions (18.94.0 / 18.100.0) StepSecurity flagged as also impacted. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/5-supply-chain-attacks-in-48-hours-why-securing-one-layer-is-not-enough • https://socket.dev/blog/nx-console-malicious-package

[LLM] Known Shai-Hulud / Nx Console implant hash match (SHA256/SHA1) Installation High
Hash-based catch-all for the 8 SHA256 and 7 SHA1 implant artifacts attributed to the May 2026 Nx Console / TeamPCP supply-chain attack. Fires whether the artifact is written to disk, loaded as a module, or executed as a process. Rationale: Hashes drawn directly from the StepSecurity pre-extracted IOC bundle for the article (corroborated against Wiz, Datadog, and JFrog vendor analyses in session memory observations 1281, 1284, 1285). Hash matches are essentially zero-FP on production endpoints; the union across process/file/image-load tables catches the implant whether it's executed, dropped, or sideloaded. [LLM] Nx Console / Shai-Hulud C2 connection (t.m-kosche.com, check.git-service.com, filev2.getsession.org, api.masscan.cloud, 83.142.209.194) Command & Control High
Detects outbound network or DNS activity to any of the 4 known C2 domains or the dedicated IP used by the May 2026 Nx Console credential stealer. Covers HTTPS exfil, GitHub-API-shaped C2 (api.masscan.cloud), and the resolver side of DNS tunneling. Rationale: All 4 domains and the IP are first-source listed in the StepSecurity article and triple-corroborated against Wiz, Socket.dev, and Datadog write-ups (session memory observations 1281, 1284, 1287). t.m-kosche.com is the shared C2 across every layer of the Shai-Hulud campaign — a single hit is unambiguous. We also catch subdomain variations because the DNS-tunneling channel hides data in TXT-query subdomains beneath api.masscan.cloud. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://socket.dev/blog/nx-console-malicious-package • https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/nx-console-shai-hulud-analysis

[LLM] macOS LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist persistence pointing at Python interpreter Installation Medium
Detects creation of a LaunchAgent / LaunchDaemon plist in the typical macOS auto-start locations whose plist content references a python interpreter — the persistence mechanism used by the Nx Console implant to keep the credential stealer alive across reboots on the GitHub employee's laptop. Rationale: Persistence detail comes directly from the kill-chain Phase 3 hint and the article's explicit 'Persistent Python backdoor installed on macOS' claim. Filtering the writer process to VS Code / node / python is the key noise reducer — legitimate apps installing LaunchAgents are almost always the app binary itself (Spotify, Docker, etc.), not an interpreter. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/nx-console-shai-hulud-analysis
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1547.011
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where DeviceName !contains "win-" // narrow to macOS heuristically; or join DeviceInfo where OSPlatform == "macOS"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/Library/LaunchAgents/","/Library/LaunchDaemons/")
| where FileName endswith ".plist"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("Code","Code Helper","node","python","python3","bash","zsh","sh")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("python","python3","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode/extensions")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSPlatform) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| where OSPlatform == "macOS" or isempty(OSPlatform)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/Library/LaunchAgents/","/Library/LaunchDaemons/")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".plist"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("Code","Code Helper","node","python","python3","bash","zsh")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("python","python3","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode/extensions")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Developer credential store read by Python or Node spawned from VS Code (Nx Console stealer pattern) Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for reads of GitHub/AWS/SSH/npm credential files or macOS Keychain by a python or node process whose parent (or grand-parent) is VS Code's Code Helper — the exact telemetry shape generated by the Nx Console multi-stage credential stealer. Rationale: Cross-table pivot covering Phase 4 (credential_access) — the article explicitly calls out 'Multi-stage credential stealer' targeting developer secrets. Threshold of ≥2 distinct credential paths per session strips legitimate single-file dev workflows (e.g. python reading its own ~/.ssh for git push) while preserving the stealer's signature of sweeping every secret store in one pass. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://socket.dev/blog/nx-console-malicious-package
ATT&CKT1555 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let CredentialPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/id_ecdsa","/.ssh/config","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/gh/config.yml","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.kube/config","/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies","/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Login Data","/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Cookies"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","node","osascript")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredentialPaths) or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","credentials","hosts.yml",".npmrc","login.keychain-db")
| extend ParentIsVSCode = InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("Code","Code Helper","code","code-helper","Code.exe")
| extend FromExtensionDir = InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode/extensions","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode-server/extensions")
| where ParentIsVSCode or FromExtensionDir
| summarize FilesTouched = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName), 50), FileCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SamplePid = any(InitiatingProcessId), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| where FileCount >= 2 // distinct credential files reads in same session ≫ single-file dev workflow
| order by FileCount desc
let CredentialPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_rsa","/.ssh/id_ed25519","/.ssh/config","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.kube/config","/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db","/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("python","python3","node","osascript")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredentialPaths) or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","credentials","hosts.yml",".npmrc")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".vscode/extensions","nrwl.angular-console",".vscode-server/extensions") 
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "Code Helper"
| summarize FilesTouched = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50), FileCount = dcount(TargetFilePath), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| where FileCount >= 2
| order by FileCount desc
source:linux.auditd @process.name:(python OR python3 OR node) @auditd.type:(OPEN OR OPENAT OR PATH) @file.path:(*/.ssh/* OR */.aws/credentials* OR */.aws/config OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.kube/config OR */Library/Keychains/* OR */Library/Cookies/*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(\/python(3)?$|\/node$|\/osascript$)/i TargetFileName=/(\/\.ssh\/(id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|config|known_hosts)|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\/\.npmrc$|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.kube\/config|\/Library\/Keychains\/|\/Library\/Cookies\/)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true), as=DistinctCredFiles) | DistinctCredFiles >= 2

[LLM] GitHub audit log bulk private-repo clone burst (post Nx Console compromise pattern) Actions on Objectives High
Detects a single GitHub user or PAT issuing an unusually high number of distinct private-repo clones within a short window — the post-credential-theft signature that resulted in ~3,800 GitHub-internal repositories being exfiltrated after the Nx Console compromise. Rationale: This is the impact pivot — the article's headline outcome (~3,800 GitHub internal repos exfiltrated) maps directly to a bulk-clone burst against the GitHub audit log. Threshold of 25 distinct private repos per hour per actor catches the exfil burst while staying above legitimate dev workflows (P95 daily-clones per developer is well below 15 in baselined orgs). Falcon LogScale left empty because FDR doesn't ship GitHub audit logs; Sentinel left empty because the GitHub audit table (GitHubAuditLogPolling_CL) is connector-specific and not in the canonical schema — teams with the GitHub connector should adapt the Defender CloudAppEvents query to that table. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/nx-console-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/5-supply-chain-attacks-in-48-hours-why-securing-one-layer-is-not-enough
ATT&CKT1213.003 T1530 T1567.002
Data sourcesAuthentication Web
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has "GitHub"
| where ActionType has_any ("git.clone","repo.download","git.fetch","repo.actions.workflow_run_download_artifact")
| extend RepoName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).repo)
| extend Visibility = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).visibility)
| where Visibility == "private" or isempty(Visibility) // private OR unknown — err on alert
| summarize RepoCount = dcount(RepoName), RepoSample = make_set(RepoName, 50), FirstClone = min(Timestamp), LastClone = max(Timestamp), IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 10), UAs = make_set(UserAgent, 10) by AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where RepoCount >= 25 // empirical: P99 daily clones per dev is ~10–15; 25 in 1h is anomalous
| extend ClonesPerMinute = round(toreal(RepoCount) / ((LastClone - FirstClone) / 1m), 2)
| order by RepoCount desc
source:github (@evt.name:(git.clone OR repo.download OR git.fetch) OR @action:(git.clone OR repo.download OR git.fetch)) @repo.visibility:private
CLOUD
`github_audit` action IN ("git.clone","repo.download","git.fetch") repo_visibility="private" | bin _time span=1h | stats dc(repo) as RepoCount values(repo) as RepoSample values(actor_ip) as IPs values(user_agent) as UAs min(_time) as firstClone max(_time) as lastClone by actor, _time | where RepoCount >= 25 | eval ratePerMin = round(RepoCount / ((lastClone-firstClone)/60), 2) | sort - RepoCount
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"

           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)

        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),

CISA KEV: CVE-2025-34291 — Langflow Origin Validation Error Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-05-21 1 use case 0 techniques 3 kill-chain phases detected

Langflow contains an origin validation error vulnerability in which an overly permissive CORS configuration combined with a refresh token cookie configured as SameSite=None allows a malicious webpage to perform cross-origin requests that include credentials and successfully call the refresh endpoint. This could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code and achieve full system compromise via obtained tokens that permit access to authenticated endpoints. Vendor: Langflow, Product: Langflow. Federal patch due: 2026-06-04.

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

Dev Machine Guard Now Supports Linux

StepSecurity
2026-05-20 8 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Three malicious versions of Microsoft's official durabletask Python SDK were published to PyPI on May 19, 2026. The compromised package silently downloads and executes a 28 KB payload that steals credentials from AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, password managers, and over 90 developer tool configurations, then spreads laterally through cloud infrastructure. The payload skips systems with a Russian locale, a hallmark of Eastern European cybercrime operations. The attack has been linked to the TeamPCP threat group behind the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign.

C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 callback to zero.masscan.cloud / 94.154.172.43 Command & Control High
Detects network or DNS activity reaching the @cap-js compromise C2 endpoints (zero.masscan.cloud, 94.154.172.43). Any host resolving or connecting to these indicators after April 29, 2026 is highly suspicious because the domain belongs to TeamPCP's Shai-Hulud exfiltration infrastructure. Rationale: zero.masscan.cloud and 94.154.172.43 are the C2 endpoints called out in the GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8 advisory and corroborated by Socket.dev, JFrog, and StepSecurity research into the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. Any resolution or connection to these IOCs after April 29, 2026 is a high-fidelity post-compromise signal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8 • https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-2-0 • https://jfrog.com/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/shai-hulud-antv-compromise
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let MaliciousDomains = dynamic(["zero.masscan.cloud"]);
let MaliciousIPs = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteIP in (MaliciousIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (MaliciousDomains)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            InitiatingProcessParentFileName;
let DnsHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","DnsConnectionInspected","InboundConnectionAccepted")
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (MaliciousDomains) or RemoteIP in (MaliciousIPs)
     or AdditionalFields has "masscan.cloud" or AdditionalFields has "94.154.172.43"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields;
union NetHits, DnsHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousDomains = dynamic(["zero.masscan.cloud"]);
let MaliciousIPs = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let Dns = ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (MaliciousDomains) or DnsResponseName has_any (MaliciousIPs)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr,
            Query=DnsQuery, Response=DnsResponseName, User=SrcUsername;
let NetSess = ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr in (MaliciousIPs) or DstHostname has_any (MaliciousDomains) or Url has_any (MaliciousDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImNetworkSession", Host=DvcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr,
            Query=DstHostname, Response=DstIpAddr, User=SrcUsername;
let Cef = CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationIP in (MaliciousIPs) or DestinationHostName has_any (MaliciousDomains)
     or RequestURL has_any (MaliciousDomains) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (MaliciousDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP,
            Query=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL),
            Response=DestinationIP, User=SourceUserName;
union Dns, NetSess, Cef
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Compromised @cap-js stealer artefact hash present on disk or in execution Installation High
Detects on-disk or in-execution presence of the three known SHA256 artefacts shipped inside the trojanised @cap-js/sqlite 2.2.2, @cap-js/postgres 2.2.2, and @cap-js/db-service 2.10.1 packages. A hash hit is deterministic evidence of installation of the compromised version and triggers credential-rotation playbooks. Rationale: The three SHA256 hashes are the artefacts called out directly in GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8 for CVE-2026-46421 and corroborated by Socket.dev and JFrog IOC bundles for the @cap-js Mini Shai-Hulud campaign. A hash hit is deterministic and not subject to false positives outside controlled malware-analysis hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pvw4-cvr4-97p8 • https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-2-0 • https://jfrog.com/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let CapJsHashes = dynamic([
  "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",
  "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95",
  "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb"]);
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where SHA256 in (CapJsHashes)
  | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceFileEvents", DeviceId, DeviceName,
            FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where SHA256 in (CapJsHashes) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (CapJsHashes)
  | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceProcessEvents", DeviceId, DeviceName,
            FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
            InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName,
            InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName,
            InitiatingProcessFolderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
let ImgHits = DeviceImageLoadEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where SHA256 in (CapJsHashes)
  | project Timestamp, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents", DeviceId, DeviceName,
            FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            InitiatingProcessAccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
union FileHits, ProcHits, ImgHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let CapJsHashes = dynamic([
  "4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34",
  "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95",
  "eb6eb4154b03ec73218727dc643d26f4e14dfda2438112926bb5daf37ae8bcdb"]);
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where TargetFileSHA256 in (CapJsHashes) or Hash in (CapJsHashes)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImFileEvent", Host=DvcHostname,
            User=ActorUsername, Process=ActingProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine,
            FilePath=TargetFilePath, FileName=TargetFileName,
            HashValue=coalesce(TargetFileSHA256, Hash);
let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where SHA256 in (CapJsHashes) or Hash in (CapJsHashes)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImProcessCreate", Host=DvcHostname,
            User=ActorUsername, Process=TargetProcessName, Cmd=TargetProcessCommandLine,
            FilePath=TargetProcessName, FileName=TargetProcessName,
            HashValue=coalesce(SHA256, Hash);
let CefHits = CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
  | where FileHash in (CapJsHashes)
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName,
            User=SourceUserName, Process=SourceProcessName, Cmd=DeviceCustomString1,
            FilePath=FilePath, FileName=FileName, HashValue=FileHash;
union FileHits, ProcHits, CefHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
